title: And no, it’s not related to the video game Burnout Paradise! #theatre...
transcript: So my favorite theatre piece from last year is coming back to New York next year, and it has me reflecting on the surprising overlap between commercial theatre and performance art. When we think about shows like Blue Man Group or Stomp, they played in New York for so long that people started to perceive them almost like tacky tourist fodder, things that the artsy locals would never touch. But lest we forget, in its early days, Blue Man Group was performed at La Mama, one of the most revered staples of experimental theatre. And Stomp also had its start in experimental fringe spaces in the U K. After its very first roots in actual street performance. It's really just context and marketing that turned public perception from something artsy to something populist, which I think shows that the line between highbrow and lowbrow is often much thinner than we think. So it seems fitting to me that Burnout Paradise is now going into the same venue that Blue Man Group occupied for over 30 years. Because at their core, they're not so different. I saw Burnout Paradise at the Edinburgh Fringe Festival in 2024 before it did a brief engagement in Brooklyn a few months later, and the experience honestly blew my mind. It's from the Australian group Ponycam Collective, and it features four performers on treadmills the whole time, trying to accomplish a series of tasks with the audience's help. It's this incredibly clever piece of performance art that comments on grind culture and the Sisyphean struggle of being a functioning adult in today's world. But it's also a wildly entertaining theatrical experience. And with this announcement that it's now getting a commercial off-Broadway run at the Astor Place Theatre, I can't help but wonder if it's following in the footsteps of the show that ran there for many years. Now, there's plenty of caveats to this, right? Burnout Paradise isn't as family friendly as those other shows. The nature of it is maybe not as easily suited to a long open run. I don't even know if it is planning to be an open run. It's currently selling four months worth of dates. I don't know how realistic it actually is, but I just can't help but think about could this new setting for Burnout Paradise allow it to undergo the same shift from the avant garde to the commercial that Stomp and Blue Man Group had?
